items.title: std's debounce hands `Timer::after` a NEGATIVE delay when the host is slow — node prints `TimeoutNegativeWarning: -1 is a negative number. Timeout duration was set to 1.` on stderr, and `debounce::a_burst_fires_once_with_the_last_callback_and_cancel_fires_nothing` (which asserts an empty stderr) goes red on a slow windows runner
items.body: Seen once on CI (windows shard 2, run 37877838887 at next @dfe0c5fc, the debug-48 merge, which touched nothing near it); the program's printed sequence was otherwise right. The debounce (`std::reactive`, around its `Timer::after(..)` call) computes a remaining delay as deadline minus now and can hand a negative number to the host timer when the clock moved past the deadline between the read and the call. Fix in std: clamp the remaining delay at 0 (`max(0, ..)`) before `Timer::after`, on both twins; a pin that drives the debounce with an injected clock past its deadline and asserts no stderr. The test's empty-stderr assertion is right and stays.
